To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a relativistic treatment of the nucleon is necessary to explain the nucleon’s electromagnetic form factors and that the pion cloud must be included in the relativistic model in order to reproduce the observed proton and neutron form factors.

the proton’s electric to magnetic form factor ratio, GE/GM, falls as a function of Q2, while the ratio of the second to the first moment of the proton’s transverse charge density, QF2/F2, remains approximately constant, and that the proton’s charge radius decreases with Q2.

the nucleon’s form factors are reproduced by a relativistic quark core plus pion cloud model, the nucleon’s magnetic moment is reproduced by a relativistically covariant quark core model, and the nucleons’ form factors are reproduced in terms of a quark core model with an effective charge that is a function of the quark’s momentum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electromagnetic structure of the nucleon.
the nucleon’s electromagnetic form-factors in the framework of relativistic quantum mechanics.
the nucleon structure and the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
relativistic effects, the pion cloud, and the nucleons’ internal structure are all required to explain the nucleon’s EMFFs.
relativistic effects are essential to understand the nucleon form factors.
the nucleon electromagnetic structure is a relativistic phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the pion cloud is a necessary part of any relativistic model of the nucleon and is a key ingredient in the reproduction of all of its form factors.
the proton’s GE n falls because of the pion-cloud effects, and that the QF2/F2 ratio is approximately constant because of the effects of chiral symmetry.
the nucleon is a composite of quarks and pions and a relativistic model that includes both is needed to reproduce the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleon form factors, in particular the proton GE/GM, are not simply a function of quark momentum distribution, but also the pion cloud.
the pion cloud is essential to reproduce GE and GF and the pion cloud has a strong impact on Q2.
the pion cloud is important for understanding the nucleon’s electromagnetic form factors, and that a relativistic treatment is essential.
